target_customer: Individuals and small teams who want email reminders without installing software
problem: People lose track of emails they need to follow up on or revisit later.
business_model: Freemium subscription, free with 50 active reminders a month and paid plans from $4 per month

founders.name: Reilly Sweetland
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; built software for clients including Netflix, Blue Jeans and Mozilla.

technical_complexity.rationale: Email parsing of a date in the address and scheduled resending is simple engineering, with deliverability the main hard part.

defensibility.rationale: The idea is easily copied; the site relies on longevity, a memorable address scheme and no-install simplicity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Gmail later added Nudges per a 2026 comparison article, but FollowUpThen is still operating with a 2026 copyright notice.

market_need_then: The service existed from 2010 or 2011 (The Next Web covered it in April 2011) and its site claims hundreds of thousands of users and about 30 million followups sent, which points to steady demand for simple reminders.

branding.domain_note: Uses followupthen.com, whose name is also the mechanism: addresses such as 1hour@followupthen.com.
branding.community_and_virality: Press mentions listed on its site include Wired (2012), Huffington Post (2015) and Forbes (2020); Product Hunt lists a launch on 8 May 2014.

brand_strength.rationale: Name doubles as the product mechanism and the company lists multiple press mentions over a decade, though independent brand coverage was not found.

outcome_analysis: FollowUpThen is a solo founder email reminder utility that predates its 2017 YC batch by years, runs on a freemium subscription and appears to have grown without disclosed outside funding. It remains active in 2026 with a claimed 30 million followups sent. No acquisition or shutdown was found, and its low defensibility is offset by simplicity and a small cost base.
notes: Outcome search found no acquisition or shutdown; the Website Planet interview mentions the sale of the founder's earlier consultancy, not FollowUpThen (interview page not retrievable). Funding searches found no rounds; Latka's $500K figure is an unverified aggregator claim. Competitor searches returned only 2026 alternative lists; the 2011 Next Web article names none, so the list is empty. Founder education not found. Batch YC page says founded 2010; site claims 12 years of operation.
